newsitem.title: RUSSIA: EBRD syndicate lends $60mln to Russian supermarket.
newsitem.headline: EBRD syndicate lends $60mln to Russian supermarket.

text.p: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), in its first Russian retail sector syndicate loan, has extended a $60 million credit to a Moscow supermarket chain, the bank said on Tuesday.
The EBRD extended $42 million and a syndicate of European commercial banks loaned an additional $17.5 million to ZAO Perekrestok, part of the Alfa Consortium of companies.

"By syndicating a significant portion of the loan, the EBRD has established an important precedent for Russian domestic transactions," Noreen Doyle, EBRD Deputy Vice President for Credit and Commercial Co-Financing said in a statement.

"The four banks are providing finance on terms similar to the EBRD, reflecting both the credit quality of the sponsor and borrower as well as an improved perception by the international financial community of transactions in Russia in general."
Perekrestok, which operates Western-style supermarkets geared towards lower and middle class shoppers in Moscow suburbs, will extend its chain to 11 stores from five.
Alfa Consortium is one of the largest industrial-financial groups in Russia and includes the Alfa Eco trading group, Alfa Bank and Alfa Capital investment fund.

The four syndicate banks are Nederlandse Financierings-Maatschappij voor Ontwikkelingslanden (FMO), Cooperatieve Centrale Raiffeisen-Boerenleenbank (Rabobank), both from the Netherlands, Bank Austria and Poland's Bank Przemyslowo-Handlowy S.A. (BPH).
